title: Hummus
description: Chickpeas blended with tahini and lemon until genuinely silky.
steps: Simmer the drained chickpeas with the baking soda and water to cover for 15 minutes until the skins slip off and they mash easily. This is the single step that separates silky hummus from gritty hummus.
Drain and rinse, rubbing to remove as many skins as you can.
Blend the lemon juice, garlic and salt first and let it sit 3 minutes, then strain out the garlic solids if you want a milder result.
Add the tahini and blend until it seizes and pales, then stream in the ice water. Cold water is what makes it fluffy rather than dense.
Add the warm chickpeas and cumin and blend a full 3-4 minutes, scraping down. Longer than feels necessary is correct.
Spread in a bowl with a swirl, pour olive oil into the well and finish with paprika and parsley.

title: Baba Ganoush
description: Charred eggplant whipped with tahini and lemon. Smoke is the whole point.
steps: Char the whole eggplants directly over a gas flame or under a hot broiler, turning every few minutes, for 25-35 minutes until the skins are blackened and blistered all over and the flesh has completely collapsed.
Do not stop early. A firm eggplant means a bitter, raw-tasting dip; it should sag like a deflated balloon.
Let them cool, then split them open and scoop out the flesh, leaving the skin behind.
Drain the flesh in a colander 15 minutes. Baba ganoush is watery otherwise.
Mash it with a fork rather than blending - the texture should be rough - then fold in the tahini, lemon juice, garlic, salt and cumin.
Spread in a shallow bowl, pour olive oil over and top with parsley and pomegranate seeds.

title: Tzatziki
description: Thick yogurt with squeezed cucumber, garlic and dill.
steps: Grate the cucumber, toss it with 1 tsp salt and leave it in a sieve 15 minutes.
Then wring it out hard in a clean towel. A shocking amount of water comes out, and this is the only thing standing between you and tzatziki soup.
Stir the squeezed cucumber into the yogurt with the garlic, dill, lemon juice, olive oil, salt and white pepper.
Chill at least 1 hour so the garlic mellows and the flavors come together.
Taste again before serving - it almost always needs more salt and lemon than you first added.

title: Muhammara
description: Roasted red pepper and walnut dip with pomegranate molasses.
steps: Toast the walnuts in a dry pan 4 minutes until fragrant, then cool. Raw walnuts taste flat and slightly bitter here.
Pat the roasted peppers dry so the dip is not watery.
Pulse the walnuts, breadcrumbs and garlic in a food processor into a coarse meal.
Add the peppers, pomegranate molasses, cumin, Aleppo pepper and salt and pulse to a thick, slightly rough paste. Do not puree it smooth.
Stream in the olive oil with the motor running, then add the lemon juice.
Taste for balance - it should be sweet, tart, smoky and hot all at once. Serve with olive oil and parsley.

title: Labneh
description: Yogurt strained overnight into a thick, tangy spread. One ingredient.
steps: Stir the salt into the yogurt. Salt draws out the whey, so do not skip it.
Line a sieve with two layers of cheesecloth, set it over a bowl and spoon the yogurt in.
Gather the cloth, twist it closed and refrigerate 12-24 hours. The longer it drains, the firmer it gets - 12 hours gives a spread, 24 gives something you can roll into balls.
Discard the whey, or save it for bread dough.
Spread the labneh in a shallow bowl, make a well with the back of a spoon and fill it with olive oil.
Scatter the za'atar, lemon zest and mint over and serve with warm pita.

title: Whipped Feta
description: Feta and yogurt blitzed into a light, salty cloud with honey and chile.
steps: Use block feta in brine, not pre-crumbled. Crumbled feta is dry and will never whip smooth.
Blitz the feta, yogurt, olive oil, lemon juice, garlic and pepper in a food processor for 2-3 minutes, scraping down twice, until completely smooth and airy.
Taste before adding any salt - feta usually brings enough.
Spread thickly on a plate with the back of a spoon, leaving ridges.
Drizzle with honey, scatter the pepper flakes and dill, and add more olive oil. Serve with warm pita or raw vegetables.

title: Tabbouleh
description: A parsley salad with a little bulgur - not the other way around.
ingredients: 4 cups flat-leaf parsley, very finely chopped
4 Roma tomatoes, seeded and finely diced
steps: Soak the fine bulgur in 1/2 cup cold water for 20-30 minutes until tender, then squeeze out any excess. Fine bulgur needs no cooking.
Chop the parsley by hand with a sharp knife, as finely as you can manage. A food processor bruises it into green paste.
This is a herb salad with bulgur as seasoning, not a grain salad - keep the proportions.
Combine the bulgur, parsley, mint, tomatoes and scallions.
Whisk the lemon juice, oil, salt, pepper and allspice and pour it over.
Let it stand 20 minutes before serving so the bulgur absorbs the dressing. Taste and add more lemon.

title: Fattoush
description: Chopped salad with fried pita shards and a sumac-lemon dressing.
ingredients: 1/4 cup olive oil, for the pita
steps: Toss the torn pita with 1/4 cup oil and a pinch of salt and bake at 400F for 10-12 minutes until crisp and golden. Let them cool completely so they stay crunchy.
Whisk the remaining oil, lemon juice, sumac, pomegranate molasses, salt and pepper. Sumac is what makes fattoush taste like fattoush - there is no good substitute.
Combine the romaine, tomatoes, cucumber, onion, radishes, parsley and mint in a wide bowl.
Dress the vegetables and toss well.
Add the pita shards at the very last moment and toss once. Added early they go soft, and the contrast is the entire reason for the dish.
Serve immediately.

title: Greek Salad
description: Tomato, cucumber, onion, olives and a slab of feta. No lettuce.
steps: Cut the vegetables in large, rustic pieces. A true horiatiki is chunky, and there is no lettuce in it.
Put the tomatoes, cucumbers, onion and pepper in a wide bowl and season with the salt and pepper.
Whisk the oil, vinegar and oregano and pour it over, tossing gently.
Scatter the olives and capers over the top.
Set the feta on top as a single slab rather than crumbling it, then drizzle with more oil and dust with oregano.
Serve at room temperature with bread to mop the juices, which are half the dish.

title: Dolmades
description: Grape leaves rolled around herbed rice and simmered in lemon.
ingredients: 1 jar (16 oz) grape leaves in brine
steps: Rinse the grape leaves well and soak in hot water 10 minutes to soften, then drain and separate them.
Cook the onions in half the oil 10 minutes, then stir in the uncooked rice, herbs, scallions, pine nuts, currants, salt and pepper. The rice stays raw - it cooks inside the rolls.
Lay a leaf vein-side up, put a teaspoon of filling near the stem end, fold the sides in and roll up firmly but not tightly. The rice swells, and an overstuffed roll bursts.
Line a heavy pot with torn or spare leaves, then pack the rolls in seam-side down in tight layers.
Pour over the remaining oil, the lemon juice and the water, and set a heatproof plate directly on top to weigh them down.
Cover and simmer very gently 50-60 minutes until the rice is tender. Cool in the pot before serving at room temperature.

title: Spanakopita
description: Spinach and feta between layers of buttered phyllo, baked shattering-crisp.
steps: Squeeze the thawed spinach dry in handfuls, as hard as you can. Any water left makes the bottom phyllo soggy, which is the usual failure of this dish.
Cook the onions in the olive oil 10 minutes until soft, then cool.
Mix the spinach, feta, ricotta, eggs, cooked onions, scallions, dill, nutmeg, salt and pepper.
Brush a 9x13 pan with butter and layer 8 sheets of phyllo, brushing each one. Keep the unused stack under a damp towel - phyllo dries out and cracks within minutes.
Spread the filling, then layer 8 more buttered sheets on top. Tuck the edges down and brush the top generously.
Score the top layers into squares with a sharp knife, then bake at 375F for 45-50 minutes until deep golden. Rest 20 minutes before cutting through.

title: Saganaki
description: A slab of firm cheese fried until the crust forms, finished with lemon.
ingredients: 12 oz kefalograviera or halloumi, in 1/2-inch slabs
steps: Pat the cheese slabs dry, then dip them briefly in water and dredge in flour, shaking off the excess. The damp-then-floured coating is what gives you a crust instead of a puddle.
Heat the oil in a small heavy skillet until it shimmers. The pan must be properly hot or the cheese melts before it browns.
Fry the cheese 1-2 minutes per side until a deep golden crust forms and the center just begins to soften.
Flip once only, with a thin spatula.
Serve straight from the pan with a hard squeeze of lemon, black pepper and oregano. Eat it immediately - it turns rubbery as it cools.

title: Falafel
description: Dried chickpeas ground raw with herbs and fried - never canned, never cooked.
steps: Soak the dried chickpeas in plenty of cold water for 18-24 hours, then drain and dry well. Do not cook them, and do not use canned chickpeas - cooked chickpeas make a paste that disintegrates in the oil.
Pulse the drained raw chickpeas with the onion, herbs and garlic in a food processor until it resembles coarse wet sand that holds together when squeezed.
Add the cumin, coriander, cayenne and salt and pulse again. Refrigerate the mixture 1 hour.
Just before frying, mix in the baking powder and flour.
Heat 3 inches of oil to 350F. Form a test ball and fry it - if it falls apart, work in another tablespoon of flour.
Fry in batches 3-4 minutes until deep brown and crisp. Drain on a rack and serve hot in pita with tahini sauce.

title: Pita Bread
description: Rounds that puff into pockets in a screaming-hot oven.
steps: Mix the flour, water, yeast, salt, sugar and oil and knead 8-10 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Rise 1 to 1 1/2 hours until doubled.
Divide into 8 pieces, shape into balls and rest 20 minutes, covered. Resting is what lets them roll out without springing back.
Heat the oven to 500F with a baking steel or inverted sheet pan inside for 45 minutes. The puff depends entirely on a fiercely hot surface.
Roll each ball into a 1/4-inch round. Do not let the rounds dry out or dust them heavily with flour.
Bake two at a time directly on the hot surface for 3-4 minutes. They should balloon within 60 seconds. Stack the finished breads in a towel so they stay soft.

title: Chicken Souvlaki
description: Lemon-oregano marinated chicken skewers grilled hot and fast.
ingredients: 2 1/2 lb boneless chicken thighs, cut in cubes
steps: Whisk the oil, lemon juice, garlic, oregano, vinegar, salt, pepper and paprika and marinate the chicken 2 hours. Use thighs rather than breast - they stay juicy over high heat.
Soak the wooden skewers in water 30 minutes so they do not burn through.
Thread the chicken on, leaving a small gap between pieces so the heat reaches all sides.
Grill over medium-high 12-15 minutes, turning every 3-4 minutes, until charred at the edges and 175F inside.
Rest 5 minutes while you warm the pita on the grill for 30 seconds a side.
Serve the skewers in the pita with tzatziki, onion and tomato.

title: Pork Souvlaki
description: The Greek street standard: marinated pork cubes grilled on skewers.
ingredients: 2 1/2 lb pork shoulder, cut in cubes
steps: Cut the pork shoulder into even 1 1/2-inch cubes, leaving some fat on - it bastes the meat as it grills.
Marinate in the oil, lemon juice, garlic, oregano, thyme, salt and pepper for 2 hours or overnight.
Soak the skewers in water 30 minutes, then thread the pork on.
Grill over medium-high 14-16 minutes, turning every 4 minutes, until charred outside and 145F at the center.
Rest 5 minutes - this matters more with pork than with chicken.
Serve wrapped in warm pita with tzatziki, onion and, as in Athens, a few French fries tucked inside.

title: Chicken Gyros
description: Stacked marinated chicken roasted into a loaf, then shaved thin.
steps: Whisk the yogurt, oil, lemon juice, garlic and all the spices into a marinade and coat the chicken. Refrigerate at least 4 hours, ideally overnight. The yogurt tenderizes the meat as well as seasoning it.
Stack the marinated thighs tightly in a loaf pan, pressing down hard to eliminate air gaps.
Roast at 350F for 1.5 hours until the center reads 175F and the top is browned.
Pour off the juices, then let the loaf rest 20 minutes. Chilling it completely makes slicing much easier if you have the time.
Turn the loaf out and shave it into thin slices with a sharp knife.
Crisp the slices in a hot dry skillet for 2 minutes - this is what gives you the browned edges of a real gyro. Serve in warm pita with tzatziki, tomato and onion.

title: Moussaka
description: Eggplant, spiced lamb and a thick bechamel baked into layers.
steps: Salt the eggplant slices and drain 45 minutes, then pat dry. Brush with oil and roast at 425F for 25 minutes until golden. Roasting rather than frying keeps the dish from being a grease bomb.

Brown the lamb, then add the onions for 8 minutes and the garlic for 1. Add the tomato paste, tomatoes, wine, cinnamon, allspice, oregano, salt and pepper and simmer 30 minutes until very thick. Watery meat sauce ruins the layers.
Make the bechamel: melt the butter, whisk in the flour and cook 2 minutes, then add the warm milk gradually and simmer until it is thick enough to hold a line, 6-8 minutes. Season with nutmeg.

Take the bechamel off the heat, let it cool 5 minutes, then whisk in the egg yolks and half the cheese. Adding yolks to boiling sauce scrambles them; they are what sets the top into a custard rather than a sauce.
Layer in a deep 9x13 dish: eggplant, meat sauce, eggplant, then all the bechamel on top. Scatter the remaining cheese.
Bake at 350F for 50-60 minutes until the top is deep golden and set. Rest a full 45 minutes before cutting - moussaka cut hot will not hold a square.

title: Pastitsio
description: Greek baked pasta with cinnamon-spiced beef under a bechamel crust.
steps: Boil the pasta 2 minutes short of al dente, drain and toss with a little butter and a handful of the cheese so the strands stay separate.

Brown the beef, add the onions for 8 minutes and the garlic for 1, then the tomato paste, tomatoes, wine, cinnamon, allspice, salt and pepper. Simmer 30 minutes until thick. The cinnamon is what makes this Greek rather than Italian.
Make a thick bechamel with the butter, flour and warm milk, cooking 8 minutes until it coats a spoon heavily. Season with nutmeg.
Off the heat, whisk in the egg yolks and half the remaining cheese.
Layer in a deep 9x13 dish: half the pasta, all the meat sauce, the rest of the pasta, then the bechamel spread to the edges to seal.
Scatter the last cheese and bake at 350F for 45-50 minutes until browned and puffed. Rest 30 minutes before cutting.

title: Greek Lemon Oregano Chicken
description: A whole chicken roasted over potatoes in lemon, garlic and oregano.
ingredients: 1 whole chicken (4 1/2 lb), cut in 8 pieces
3 lb Yukon gold potatoes, cut in wedges
steps: Heat the oven to 425F. Whisk the oil, lemon juice, garlic, oregano, salt and pepper.
Toss the potato wedges with two thirds of the mixture in a large roasting pan and spread them out in one layer.
Pat the chicken dry, rub with the remaining mixture and set it skin-side up on top of the potatoes so the fat bastes them as it renders.
Pour the broth into the pan around the potatoes, not over the chicken skin, and tuck the lemon slices in.
Roast 45 minutes, then baste the potatoes with the pan juices and roast 30-40 minutes more, until the chicken reads 175F in the thigh and the potatoes are browned and soft.
Rest 10 minutes and serve with the pan juices spooned over.

title: Greek Lemon Potatoes
description: Potatoes roasted in lemon, oregano and broth until creamy inside and browned outside.
ingredients: 3 lb Yukon gold potatoes, cut in thick wedges
steps: Heat the oven to 425F. Put the potato wedges in a single layer in a roasting pan - crowding them means steaming instead of browning.
Pour over the oil, lemon juice and broth and add the garlic, oregano, salt and pepper. The liquid should come about a third of the way up.
Roast 45 minutes, turning the potatoes once at the halfway point.
Roast 25-30 minutes more, until the liquid has cooked away almost entirely and the potatoes are deeply browned on the bottom.
That transition from braising to roasting is the whole technique: the potatoes cook through in the lemony broth, then fry in the oil left behind.
Scrape up all the browned bits from the pan and finish with parsley.

title: Keftedes
description: Greek meatballs with mint and oregano, fried crisp outside.
steps: Soak the breadcrumbs in the milk 5 minutes. Squeeze the grated onion dry in a towel - its water would otherwise make the mix too loose to fry.
Mix both meats with the soaked breadcrumbs, onion, garlic, egg, mint, parsley, oregano, vinegar, salt and pepper. Mint and oregano together are what make these Greek.
Refrigerate the mixture 1 hour so it firms up and the flavors settle.
Roll into walnut-sized balls, flatten them slightly, and dust lightly with flour.
Fry in the olive oil over medium-high, in batches, 3-4 minutes per side until deeply browned and cooked through.
Drain on a rack and serve hot with lemon wedges and tzatziki.

title: Greek Baked Chicken and Orzo
description: One pan of chicken, orzo and tomato baked together with feta on top.
steps: Season the chicken and brown it skin-side down in the oil in an oven-safe pan, 7 minutes, then 3 on the other side. Set it aside.
Cook the onion in the rendered fat 6 minutes, then the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the orzo and toast 2 minutes, then the tomatoes, broth, oregano and cinnamon.
Nestle the chicken back on top, skin-side up and above the liquid so it stays crisp.
Bake uncovered at 400F for 35-40 minutes until the orzo is tender and the chicken reads 175F. Scatter the olives in for the last 10 minutes.
Crumble the feta over, add the dill, and serve with lemon wedges.

title: Avgolemono
description: Greek chicken soup thickened with an egg and lemon emulsion.
steps: Simmer the broth with the rice for 18-20 minutes until the rice is fully tender. Then take the pot off the heat and let it stop bubbling.
Whisk the eggs in a bowl until completely frothy, then whisk in the lemon juice.

Now temper: ladle one cup of the hot broth into the eggs in a very thin stream while whisking constantly. Then do it again with a second cup. Rushing this is the only way to fail at avgolemono - the eggs will scramble into threads.
Pour the tempered mixture back into the pot, stirring continuously.
Return to the lowest possible heat for 2-3 minutes, stirring, until it thickens slightly and turns opaque and pale yellow. It must never boil again.
Add the chicken, salt and white pepper and heat through. Serve with dill and lemon slices.

title: Chicken Shawarma
description: Spiced yogurt-marinated chicken roasted hot and sliced thin.
steps: Whisk the yogurt, oil, lemon juice, garlic and all the spices into a thick marinade and coat the chicken thoroughly.
Refrigerate at least 4 hours and up to 24. This spice blend needs time to penetrate, and the yogurt tenderizes as it sits.
Spread the thighs in a single layer on a sheet pan - do not crowd them, or they steam instead of browning.
Roast at 425F for 35-40 minutes, until the edges are charred and the meat reads 175F.
Rest 10 minutes, then slice across the grain into thin strips.
Serve in warm pita with tahini sauce, tomato, onion and pickled turnips.

title: Beef Kofta Kebabs
description: Spiced ground beef pressed onto skewers and grilled over high heat.
ingredients: 1 yellow onion, grated and squeezed dry
steps: Squeeze the grated onion bone dry in a towel. Wet onion is why kofta slide off skewers.

Knead the beef with the onion, garlic, herbs, spices, salt and pepper for a full 3 minutes - longer than you would for meatballs. The mixture should become sticky and slightly paste-like, which is what makes it cling to the skewer.
Chill 1 hour.
Take a handful and press it around a flat metal skewer into a long sausage shape about 1 inch thick, squeezing firmly along its length. Flat skewers grip the meat; round ones let it spin.
Grill over high heat 10-12 minutes, turning every 3 minutes, until charred outside and just cooked through.
Rest 5 minutes, then slide off the skewers into warm pita with tahini sauce.

title: Shish Tawook
description: Yogurt and lemon marinated chicken skewers, Lebanon's standard grill.
steps: Whisk the yogurt, lemon juice, oil, garlic, tomato paste and spices into a marinade.
Coat the chicken cubes and refrigerate 4 hours or overnight. The yogurt's acid and enzymes keep lean breast meat tender over fierce heat - skip it and you get dry cubes.
Thread the chicken onto skewers, pressing the pieces close but not packed tight.
Grill over high heat 10-12 minutes, turning every 3 minutes, until lightly charred and 165F inside. Do not overcook; breast meat gives you a narrow window.
Rest 5 minutes.
Serve with toum and warm pita.

title: Mujadara
description: Lentils and rice under a mountain of deeply caramelized onions.
steps: Fry the sliced onions in the olive oil over medium heat for 30-40 minutes, stirring often, until deeply browned and some pieces are genuinely crisp. This takes far longer than seems reasonable and is the entire flavor of the dish - do not stop at golden.
Lift out a third of the onions onto paper towels to stay crisp for the top.
Simmer the lentils in the water for 15 minutes until almost tender but still firm.
Add the rice, the remaining onions with their oil, the spices and salt to the lentil pot. The water should sit about an inch above the rice.
Cover and cook on the lowest heat 18-20 minutes without stirring, then rest off the heat 10 minutes.
Fluff with a fork, pile the reserved crisp onions on top, and serve with yogurt and parsley.

title: Shakshuka
description: Eggs poached in a spiced tomato and pepper sauce, served from the pan.
steps: Cook the onion and bell peppers in the oil over medium-high 10 minutes until soft and lightly charred at the edges.
Add the garlic, tomato paste and all the spices and cook 2 minutes to bloom them.
Add the tomatoes and salt and simmer 12-15 minutes until thick enough that a spoon dragged through leaves a trail. A loose sauce will not hold the eggs in place.
Make 6 wells with the back of a spoon and crack an egg into each.
Cover and cook 6-8 minutes, until the whites are just set and the yolks still run. Check at 6 - they overcook fast.
Scatter the feta and cilantro over and bring the pan to the table with warm pita for scooping.

title: Shorbat Adas
description: Red lentil soup with cumin and lemon, blended smooth. Pantry to bowl in 40 minutes.
steps: Cook the onion and carrots in the oil 8 minutes, then add the garlic and all the spices for 1 minute.
Add the rinsed red lentils and the broth and bring to a boil, skimming any foam.
Simmer 25 minutes until the lentils have completely collapsed. Red lentils are meant to fall apart - that is what thickens the soup.
Blend until smooth, or partly blend if you want some texture.
Add the salt and lemon juice off the heat. The lemon is not a garnish; without it the soup tastes flat and heavy.
Serve with cilantro and toasted pita, and more lemon on the side.

title: Kibbeh
description: Bulgur and beef shells stuffed with spiced lamb and pine nuts, deep-fried.
ingredients: 1 tbsp ground allspice, for the filling
steps: Soak the fine bulgur in cold water 30 minutes, then squeeze it bone dry. Any moisture left and the shells will crack open in the oil.
Make the filling: brown the lamb, add the diced onions and cook 10 minutes, then the pine nuts, butter, allspice and salt. Cook until quite dry and cool completely.
Process the lean beef with the quartered onion, allspice, cinnamon, salt and pepper into a smooth paste, then knead in the squeezed bulgur until it holds together like clay. Chill 30 minutes.
Wet your hands. Take a golf-ball of the shell mixture, press your index finger into it and rotate to hollow it into a thin-walled cup - aim for 1/4 inch walls.
Spoon in the filling, pinch the opening closed and smooth it into a football shape with pointed ends. Any crack must be sealed with wet fingers.
Fry in 350F oil for 5-6 minutes until deep brown and crisp. Drain on a rack and serve with yogurt.

title: Manakish Za'atar
description: Flatbread spread with za'atar and olive oil, baked until the edges crisp.
ingredients: 3/4 cup olive oil, for the topping
steps: Mix the flour, water, yeast, salt, sugar and 3 tbsp oil and knead 8 minutes until smooth. Rise 1 1/2 hours until doubled.
Stir the za'atar with the 3/4 cup olive oil into a loose, spreadable paste. It should look wet - dry za'atar scorches in the oven.
Heat the oven to 450F with a baking steel or sheet pan inside.
Divide the dough into 6 and roll each into a 1/4-inch round. Rest 10 minutes.
Spread the za'atar paste over each round, leaving a 1/2-inch border, and dimple it with your fingertips so the oil pools.
Bake 8-10 minutes until the edges are golden and the topping is bubbling. Serve warm with labneh, cucumber and mint.

title: Batata Harra
description: Crisp fried potatoes tossed with garlic, cilantro and chile.
ingredients: 3 lb russet potatoes, cut in 1-inch cubes
steps: Soak the cubed potatoes in cold water 10 minutes, then drain and dry them thoroughly. Surface starch and water both prevent crisping.
Toss with half the oil and the salt and roast at 450F for 30-35 minutes, turning once, until deeply browned and crisp.

While they roast, warm the remaining oil with the garlic, pepper flakes and coriander over low heat 3 minutes, just until the garlic is fragrant and pale gold. Burnt garlic will make the whole dish bitter.
Tip the hot potatoes into a bowl and pour the garlic oil over.
Add the cilantro, lemon juice and black pepper and toss hard while everything is still hot.
Taste for salt and serve immediately.

title: Toum
description: Lebanese garlic sauce whipped into a fluffy white emulsion. No dairy, no eggs.
steps: Trim any green germs from the garlic cloves - they are the bitter part.
Process the garlic with the salt until completely pureed, scraping down several times.
Now add the oil one tablespoon at a time with the motor running, alternating with a teaspoon of lemon juice. This is slower than it sounds and must not be rushed.
Once about a cup of oil is in and the mixture has turned thick and white, you can pour the rest in a thin steady stream.
If it breaks and turns soupy, start again with one fresh garlic clove in a clean bowl and dribble the broken mixture into it as if it were oil.
Finish with the ice water to lighten and stabilize it. It keeps a month refrigerated and mellows over the first few days - fresh toum is ferociously sharp.

title: Roasted Cauliflower with Tahini
description: Charred cauliflower under lemony tahini with pomegranate and herbs.
ingredients: 2 large heads cauliflower, cut in florets
steps: Heat the oven to 450F. Toss the florets with the oil, cumin, coriander, salt and pepper.
Spread them cut-side down in a single layer on a sheet pan. Contact with hot metal is what gives you the browned faces; a crowded pan steams them pale.
Roast 30-35 minutes without stirring for the first 20, until deeply charred in spots and tender.
Whisk the tahini, lemon juice and garlic - it will seize and look ruined, which is normal - then whisk in the ice water a tablespoon at a time until it loosens into a pourable cream.
Spread the tahini sauce on a platter and pile the hot cauliflower on top.
Finish with pomegranate seeds, parsley and pine nuts.

title: Lamb Kofta with Yogurt Sauce
description: Spiced lamb patties seared and served over garlicky yogurt.
ingredients: 1 yellow onion, grated and squeezed dry
3 cloves garlic, minced, for the sauce
steps: Squeeze the grated onion completely dry, then knead it into the lamb with the garlic, herbs, spices and salt for 3 minutes until sticky.
Chill 1 hour - lamb is soft and the patties hold their shape far better cold.
Form into 18 oval patties about 3/4 inch thick.
Sear in the olive oil over medium-high, 4 minutes per side, in batches. Do not press them down; you want the juices inside.
Stir the yogurt with the extra garlic, lemon juice and a pinch of salt and spread it across a platter.
Set the hot kofta on the yogurt, scatter the pine nuts and sumac over and serve with pita.

title: Mahshi Stuffed Peppers
description: Bell peppers filled with spiced rice and lamb, baked in tomato broth.
ingredients: 6 large bell peppers, tops cut off and seeded
steps: Mix the raw lamb, rinsed raw rice, onion, garlic, half the tomato paste, the spices, herbs, salt and pepper. The rice goes in uncooked - it swells inside the pepper, so fill only two thirds full or they burst.
Stand the peppers in a deep baking dish and spoon the filling in loosely, replacing the cut-off tops as lids.
Whisk the crushed tomatoes, broth, the remaining tomato paste and the olive oil and pour it around the peppers so it comes a third of the way up.
Cover tightly with foil and bake at 375F for 60 minutes.
Uncover and bake 15 minutes more, basting the peppers with the sauce once, until they are soft and lightly browned on top and the rice is tender.
Rest 10 minutes and serve with the sauce spooned over and yogurt on the side.

title: Ful Medames
description: Stewed fava beans mashed with lemon, cumin and olive oil. Egypt's breakfast.
ingredients: 2 cans (15 oz each) fava beans, drained
steps: Warm the drained favas with 1/2 cup water in a saucepan over medium heat 10 minutes.
Add half the olive oil, the garlic, cumin and cayenne and cook 5 more minutes.
Mash about half the beans directly in the pan with a fork or potato masher, leaving the rest whole. The mix of textures is the point.
Stir in the lemon juice and salt. Taste - ful needs a lot of both lemon and salt to come alive.
Spoon into bowls and pour the remaining olive oil over generously.
Top with tomato, red onion, parsley and quartered eggs, and serve with warm pita.

title: Adana Kebab
description: Hand-minced lamb with red pepper pressed onto wide skewers and grilled.
ingredients: 1 red bell pepper, very finely minced
steps: The fat content matters: ask the butcher for lamb shoulder with about 20 percent fat. Lean lamb makes dry, crumbly kebabs.
Knead the lamb with the minced pepper, Aleppo pepper, cumin, salt and pepper for 5 full minutes until it turns tacky and binds to itself.
Chill 1 hour, then wet your hands and press the mixture along wide flat skewers in a long even strip, squeezing it on firmly and ridging it with your fingers.
Grill over hot coals 10-12 minutes, turning every 2-3 minutes. Keep the skewers moving so the fat renders without flaring up.
Warm the lavash over the coals and grill the tomatoes and green peppers alongside.
Slide the kebabs onto the bread, then top with the onion tossed in sumac and parsley.

title: Menemen
description: Turkish scrambled eggs with tomato and green pepper, kept soft and loose.
ingredients: 4 ripe tomatoes, grated or finely chopped
steps: Cook the green peppers in the butter and oil over medium heat 8 minutes until soft.
Add the grated tomatoes, Aleppo pepper, salt and black pepper and cook 8-10 minutes until the liquid has reduced and the mixture is jammy. Watery tomato makes watery menemen.
Lower the heat right down and crack the eggs straight into the pan.
Stir slowly and gently, breaking the yolks but keeping the egg in loose ribbons rather than small curds. Menemen is meant to be soft and barely set, not dry.
Take it off the heat while it still looks slightly underdone.
Scatter the feta and parsley over and serve from the pan with crusty bread.

title: Lahmacun
description: Paper-thin flatbread with a spiced lamb topping, rolled up to eat.
steps: Mix the flour, water, yeast, salt and oil and knead 8 minutes. Rise 1 1/2 hours.
Pulse the onion, bell pepper, garlic and parsley in a food processor to a fine paste, then squeeze out the excess liquid through a sieve. Wet topping steams the dough instead of crisping it.
Mix the squeezed vegetables with the lamb, tomato paste, Aleppo pepper, cumin, paprika and salt into a loose paste.
Heat the oven to 500F with a steel or inverted sheet pan inside for 45 minutes.
Divide the dough into 8 and roll each piece as thin as you possibly can - almost transparent. Spread a very thin layer of the lamb mixture right to the edges.
Bake 6-8 minutes until the edges are crisp and the meat is cooked. Serve with lemon and a handful of parsley, rolled up like a wrap.

title: Imam Bayildi
description: Eggplant braised in olive oil with tomato and onion, served cool.
steps: Cut a deep slit lengthwise in each eggplant without cutting through, salt them inside and out and leave 30 minutes, then rinse and pat dry.
Fry the whole eggplants in half the olive oil, turning, until browned and softened on all sides, 10 minutes. Set aside.
Cook the onions in the remaining oil over medium-low for 20 minutes until completely soft and sweet, then add the garlic for 2 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, tomato paste, sugar, parsley, salt and pepper and cook 10 minutes.
Open each eggplant's slit and stuff it generously with the onion mixture. Set them in a baking dish, pour over the water and lemon juice and any remaining filling.
Cover and bake at 350F for 40 minutes. Cool to room temperature before serving - this dish is always eaten cool, and the flavor is better the next day.

title: Mercimek Corbasi
description: Silky Turkish red lentil soup finished with sizzling mint butter.
ingredients: 4 tbsp butter, for the mint butter
steps: Cook the onion, carrot and potato in the butter and oil 10 minutes, then add the garlic, tomato paste and cumin for 2 minutes.
Add the lentils and broth, bring to a boil and skim the foam.
Simmer 25 minutes until everything has collapsed, then blend completely smooth. Turkish lentil soup should be velvety, not chunky.
Season with the salt, and thin with hot water if it is thicker than heavy cream.
Make the mint butter: melt the 4 tbsp butter in a small pan until it foams, take it off the heat and stir in the dried mint and Aleppo pepper. It will sizzle and turn red - do not let it burn.
Ladle the soup into bowls and drizzle the mint butter over each one. Serve with lemon to squeeze in.

title: Turkish Rice Pilaf
description: Butter-toasted rice and orzo steamed into separate, glossy grains.
steps: Rinse the rice in several changes of water until it runs clear, then soak it in warm salted water 15 minutes and drain. This soaking is the Turkish step that gives you long, separate grains.
Toast the orzo in the butter and oil over medium heat 4-5 minutes until golden brown. Watch it closely; it colors fast.
Add the drained rice and stir 2 minutes to coat every grain in fat.
Pour in the hot broth, add the salt and pepper and bring to a boil.
Cover, lower to the barest heat and cook 15 minutes without lifting the lid once.
Take it off the heat, lay a clean towel under the lid and rest 10 minutes - the towel absorbs condensation that would otherwise make the rice damp. Fluff with a fork.

title: Spinach and Feta Borek
description: Coiled phyllo pastry filled with cheese and spinach, baked golden.
ingredients: 1 lb frozen spinach, thawed and squeezed dry
steps: Squeeze the spinach completely dry, then mix it with the feta, ricotta, eggs, dill and pepper. Taste before salting - feta is usually enough.
Whisk the olive oil and milk together; this thinner mixture brushes on more evenly than oil alone and keeps the layers tender.
Lay one phyllo sheet out and brush it with the oil mixture. Keep the rest under a damp towel or it dries and shatters within minutes.
Spread a line of filling along one long edge and roll it into a loose rope.
Coil the rope in the center of an oiled round pan, then make more ropes and coil them around the first to form a spiral.
Brush the top with egg yolk, scatter the sesame and nigella seeds and bake at 375F for 40-45 minutes until deep golden. Rest 15 minutes before cutting.

title: Cilbir
description: Poached eggs on garlic yogurt under sizzling Aleppo pepper butter.
steps: Stir the yogurt with the garlic and salt and let it sit at room temperature while you work. Cold yogurt straight from the fridge chills the eggs and ruins the dish - it should be cool, not cold.
Bring a wide pan of water to a bare simmer with the vinegar.
Crack each egg through a fine sieve first to drain the loose white, then slip them into the water and poach 3 minutes for runny yolks.
Spread the yogurt across two shallow bowls in a thick layer.
Melt the butter until it foams and just begins to brown, take it off the heat and stir in the Aleppo pepper and paprika.
Set the drained eggs on the yogurt, pour the red butter over and finish with dill. Serve with toast.

title: Chicken Tagine with Olives and Preserved Lemon
description: Saffron and ginger chicken braised slowly with green olives.
steps: Steep the saffron in 2 tbsp hot water for 10 minutes. This small step pulls far more color and flavor out than crumbling it in dry.
Brown the chicken skin-side down in the oil 7 minutes, then set aside.
Cook the onions in the same pot 10 minutes until soft, then add the garlic, fresh ginger and all the ground spices for 2 minutes.
Return the chicken, add the broth and saffron water, cover and simmer very gently 45 minutes.
Add the preserved lemon and olives and cook uncovered 15 minutes more, until the sauce has reduced and thickened and the chicken is falling off the bone.
Taste before salting - the preserved lemons and olives are both salty. Finish with the herbs and serve with couscous or bread.

title: Lamb Tagine with Apricots
description: Slow-braised lamb with dried apricots, cinnamon and almonds.
ingredients: 3 lb lamb shoulder, cut in chunks
steps: Season the lamb and brown it hard in the oil in batches. Crowding the pot steams the meat and you lose the foundation of the dish.
Cook the onions 10 minutes, then add the garlic, ginger and all the ground spices for 2 minutes.
Return the lamb with the broth, bring to a bare simmer, cover and cook 1 1/2 hours.
Add the apricots and honey and cook uncovered 30-40 minutes more, until the lamb pulls apart and the sauce is syrupy.
Taste and balance: this should be sweet, savory and warm with spice all at once. Add more honey or a squeeze of lemon as needed.
Scatter the toasted almonds and cilantro over and serve over couscous.

title: Seven-Vegetable Couscous
description: Steamed couscous under a saffron-spiced vegetable and chickpea broth.
steps: Pour the boiling 3 1/2 cups broth over the couscous in a bowl, cover tightly and leave 10 minutes, then fork in the butter and fluff thoroughly. Breaking up every clump with your fingers is what keeps it light.
Cook the onions in the oil 8 minutes, then the garlic and all the spices for 2 minutes.
Add the carrots, turnips, squash, chickpeas, tomatoes and the 6 cups broth and simmer 20 minutes.
Add the zucchini and cook 10 minutes more, until all the vegetables are tender but still holding their shape.
Season and stir in the cilantro.
Mound the couscous in a wide bowl, make a well, and ladle the vegetables and plenty of broth into it. Serve harissa on the side so everyone sets their own heat.

title: Harissa Roast Chicken
description: Chicken rubbed with harissa and honey, roasted over lemons and chickpeas.
steps: Whisk the harissa, oil, honey, lemon juice, garlic, cumin, salt and pepper into a paste. Harissa brands vary enormously in heat, so taste yours and adjust.
Rub two thirds of it all over the chicken, getting some under the skin.
Toss the chickpeas and red onions with the remaining paste and spread them in a roasting pan with the lemon slices.
Set the chicken on top, skin-side up, so it sits above the chickpeas and the skin crisps.
Roast at 425F for 45-55 minutes until the skin is dark and lacquered and the thigh reads 175F. The honey will char at the edges, which is what you want.
Rest 10 minutes, then finish with cilantro and serve with yogurt to cool the heat.

title: Chermoula Baked Fish
description: White fish under a herb, garlic and paprika marinade, baked on potatoes.
steps: Blend the cilantro, parsley, garlic, oil, lemon juice and spices into the chermoula - a loose, bright green paste.
Coat the fish in a third of it and refrigerate 30 minutes while you prepare the vegetables. Do not marinate fish much longer in this much acid or the flesh goes chalky.
Toss the potato slices with another third of the chermoula and spread them in a baking dish. Bake at 400F for 25 minutes until nearly tender.
Lay the tomato and pepper slices over the potatoes, then the fish on top.
Spoon the remaining chermoula over and add the lemon slices.
Bake 18-20 minutes until the fish flakes at the thickest point. Serve from the dish with all the pan juices.

title: Moroccan Carrot Salad
description: Cooked carrots dressed warm with cumin, lemon and harissa.
ingredients: 2 lb carrots, sliced in thick rounds
steps: Boil the carrot rounds in salted water 8-10 minutes until just tender - a knife should meet slight resistance. Mushy carrots fall apart in the dressing.
Drain and leave them in the colander for a minute to steam dry.
Warm the olive oil with the garlic, cumin and paprika over low heat 2 minutes until fragrant.
Pour the warm spiced oil over the hot carrots along with the harissa, lemon juice and salt, and toss. Dressing them hot is what lets them absorb the flavor rather than just wearing it.
Cool to room temperature, then fold in the cilantro and parsley.
Taste again before serving - it will want more lemon and salt once cooled.

title: Harira
description: Moroccan lentil, chickpea and tomato soup thickened with flour and herbs.
steps: Brown the lamb in the oil, then add the onions and celery and cook 10 minutes.
Add the garlic and all the spices and cook 2 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, lentils, chickpeas and broth and simmer 50 minutes until the lentils are soft and the lamb is tender.
Whisk the flour with 1 cup of cold water until completely smooth - any lumps here become lumps in the soup.
Pour it into the simmering pot in a thin stream while stirring constantly, then cook 10 minutes more. The soup should turn velvety and slightly thickened.
Stir in the herbs, salt and lemon juice off the heat. Serve with dates on the side, as is traditional during Ramadan.

title: Zaalouk
description: Moroccan cooked salad of eggplant and tomato, mashed and spiced.
steps: Put the eggplant, tomatoes, oil, garlic and spices in a wide pan with 1/2 cup water, cover and cook over medium heat 20 minutes.
Uncover and cook 15-20 minutes more, stirring and mashing with a wooden spoon as you go, until everything collapses and the liquid cooks away.
Keep going until the oil separates out and the mixture pulls away from the pan. Stopping while it is still wet gives you a watery dip rather than zaalouk.
Mash it coarsely - it should be rough, not pureed.
Stir in the salt, lemon juice and herbs off the heat.
Serve warm or at room temperature with pita. It keeps four days and improves overnight.

title: Moroccan Mint Tea
description: Gunpowder green tea steeped with a fistful of mint and poured from a height.
steps: Put the tea leaves in a teapot, add 1 cup boiling water, swirl for 30 seconds and pour that first water off. This rinse removes the dustiness and bitterness from the leaves.
Add the rest of the boiling water and steep 3 minutes.
Stuff the mint in, stems and all, and add the sugar. Push the mint down under the liquid with a spoon.
Steep 4-5 minutes more, no longer, or the mint turns bitter.
Pour a glass, return it to the pot, and repeat twice to mix and aerate the tea.
Serve by pouring from a foot above the glass - the height builds the foam on top, which is considered part of a properly served glass.

title: Chicken Bastilla
description: Sweet-savory spiced chicken and almond pie in phyllo, dusted with sugar.
ingredients: 2 tsp ground cinnamon, for the almonds
steps: Braise the chicken with the butter, onions, garlic, saffron, spices and broth for 50 minutes until falling off the bone. Shred the meat and discard the bones.
Reduce the remaining liquid with the onions until thick and almost dry - 20 minutes. Wet filling will turn the pastry to paste.
Stir the herbs into the reduced onion mixture, then pour in the beaten eggs and stir constantly over low heat until they set into soft curds. Take it off the heat while still moist.
Pulse the toasted almonds with the 1/2 cup powdered sugar and 2 tsp cinnamon into a coarse crumble.

Butter a round pan and layer 8 sheets of phyllo, buttering each and letting them overhang. Add the almond mixture, then the shredded chicken, then the egg mixture. Fold the overhang over and top with 6 more buttered sheets, tucking them down the sides.

Bake at 375F for 40-45 minutes until deep golden. Invert onto a plate, then dust heavily with powdered sugar and draw cinnamon lines across the top. The sweet crust over savory filling is the entire point of bastilla.

title: Grilled Whole Fish with Ladolemono
description: Whole fish grilled over high heat and dressed with lemon-oil emulsion.
ingredients: 2 whole fish (1 1/2 lb each), cleaned and scaled
1/4 cup olive oil, for the fish
steps: Pat the fish bone dry and score the skin three times on each side down to the bone. Scoring helps it cook evenly and stops the skin curling.
Rub with oil, season inside and out, and stuff the cavities with lemon slices and fresh oregano.
Get the grill very hot and clean the grates, then oil them well. A clean, hot, oiled grate is the only way whole fish comes off without tearing.
Grill 7-9 minutes per side, depending on thickness, and turn only once using two spatulas.
Whisk the remaining olive oil, lemon juice, dried oregano and salt hard until it emulsifies into a cloudy ladolemono.
Pour it over the hot fish and finish with parsley. Serve whole and let people take fillets off the bone at the table.

title: Shrimp Saganaki
description: Shrimp baked in spicy tomato sauce under melting feta.
ingredients: 1/2 cup ouzo or dry white wine
steps: Cook the onion in the oil in an oven-safe skillet 7 minutes, then add the garlic and pepper flakes for 1 minute.
Add the ouzo and let it bubble down by half, 2 minutes. The anise note is what makes this distinctly Greek.
Add the tomatoes, oregano and salt and simmer 15 minutes until thick.
Nestle the raw shrimp into the sauce in a single layer - they cook entirely in the oven, so do not pre-cook them.
Crumble the feta over the top and bake at 425F for 10-12 minutes until the shrimp are pink and the feta has softened and browned in spots.
Finish with parsley and serve straight from the pan with bread to mop the sauce.

title: Grilled Octopus
description: Octopus simmered tender for an hour, then charred fast over coals.
steps: Put the octopus in a pot with the bay leaves, onion, half the vinegar and the wine cork - Greek cooks swear the cork helps tenderize it, and it costs nothing to include. Add no water; the octopus releases plenty.
Cover and simmer very gently 60-75 minutes. It is ready when a knife slides into the thickest part of a tentacle with no resistance. Undercooked octopus is rubber, and no amount of grilling fixes it.
Let it cool in its own liquid for 20 minutes, then cut into tentacles and pat dry.
Toss with half the oil, the oregano and pepper flakes.
Grill over very hot coals 2-3 minutes per side, just long enough to char the edges and crisp the suckers.
Dress with the remaining oil, the lemon juice, remaining vinegar, flaky salt and pepper. Serve with parsley, olives and lemon wedges.

title: Roasted Salmon with Tahini
description: Spiced salmon fillets under lemon tahini with herbs and pine nuts.
steps: Heat the oven to 425F. Pat the salmon dry and rub with the oil, cumin, paprika, cayenne, salt and pepper.
Roast skin-side down on a lined sheet pan 12-14 minutes, until the thickest part reads 125F for medium. Salmon keeps cooking off the heat, so pull it early.
Whisk the tahini, lemon juice and garlic. It will seize into a thick paste, which is normal.
Whisk in the ice water a tablespoon at a time until it loosens into a pourable sauce the texture of cream.
Season the sauce with salt and taste - it should be sharply lemony to cut the richness of the fish.
Spoon it over the salmon and finish with parsley, pine nuts and sumac.

title: Seafood Paella
description: Saffron rice with shellfish and a crisp toasted crust on the bottom.
ingredients: 6 cups fish or chicken broth, hot
steps: Steep the saffron in a ladleful of the hot broth. Cook the onion and pepper in the oil in a wide shallow pan 8 minutes, then add the garlic, tomato paste and smoked paprika for 2 minutes.
Add the rice and stir 2 minutes to coat every grain.
Pour in all the hot broth with the saffron, add the salt, and shake the pan to settle the rice into an even layer.
From this point on, do not stir. Stirring makes risotto; paella needs the grains left alone so the bottom can toast.

Simmer uncovered 12 minutes, then arrange the shrimp, mussels and squid on top and cook 8-10 minutes more until the liquid is gone and the seafood is just done. Scatter the peas over for the last 3 minutes.
Listen for a faint crackle and raise the heat for 60-90 seconds at the end to form the socarrat, the caramelized crust on the bottom. Rest 5 minutes, then serve with lemon and parsley.

title: Gambas al Ajillo
description: Shrimp sizzled in garlic chile oil and brought to the table bubbling.
steps: Pat the shrimp completely dry and season with the salt.
Put the oil, sliced garlic and broken chiles in a cold skillet and bring it up over medium heat. Starting cold lets the garlic perfume the oil slowly instead of burning.
Cook 4-5 minutes until the garlic is pale gold, then add the smoked paprika for 15 seconds.
Raise the heat to high and add the shrimp in a single layer. Cook 1 minute per side, no longer.
Add the sherry and lemon juice and let it bubble 30 seconds.
Throw in the parsley and bring the pan straight to the table while it is still sizzling, with bread for the garlic oil - which is the best part.

title: Mediterranean Baked Cod
description: Cod baked over tomatoes, olives and capers in one dish.
steps: Heat the oven to 425F. Toss the tomatoes, olives, capers, onion and garlic with half the oil, the oregano, pepper flakes and half the salt in a baking dish.
Roast the vegetables alone for 12 minutes to soften them and concentrate the tomatoes. Putting the fish in from the start would overcook it.
Pat the cod dry, season with the remaining salt and pepper and set it on top of the vegetables.
Drizzle with the remaining oil and the lemon juice and tuck the lemon slices around.
Bake 12-14 minutes until the fish flakes with gentle pressure at its thickest point.
Finish with parsley and spoon the pan juices over each fillet.

title: Salade Nicoise
description: Composed salad of tuna, green beans, potatoes, egg and olives.
ingredients: 2 cans (5 oz each) tuna in olive oil
steps: Boil the potatoes in salted water 15 minutes until tender, then halve them.
Blanch the green beans in the same water 3 minutes and plunge them into ice water so they stay bright and snappy.
Lower the eggs into boiling water for 8 minutes for jammy yolks, then cool in ice water and peel.
Whisk the oil, vinegar, Dijon, garlic, salt and pepper into a vinaigrette, and toss the warm potatoes in a few spoonfuls of it right away.
Arrange everything in separate groups on a platter rather than tossing it together. A Nicoise is a composed salad, and the point is that each element stays itself.
Spoon the rest of the vinaigrette over, add the anchovies and basil, and season the eggs and tomatoes directly.

title: Bouillabaisse
description: Provencal fish stew with saffron and fennel, served with rouille toasts.
ingredients: 2 lb mixed white fish, in chunks
1 cup olive oil, for the rouille
steps: Build the base: cook the fennel and onions in the oil 12 minutes until soft, then add the garlic, saffron, fennel seeds and orange zest for 2 minutes. The orange zest and fennel together are the signature of a Marseille bouillabaisse.
Add the tomatoes, wine and fish broth and simmer 40 minutes. Strain it if you want the classic smooth broth, or leave it rustic.
Make the rouille: blend the egg yolks, roasted pepper, harissa and a clove of garlic, then stream in the cup of olive oil very slowly until it thickens like mayonnaise. Pouring too fast breaks it.
Bring the broth back to a simmer and season well. It should taste intensely of the sea before any fish goes in.
Add the firmest fish first and cook 4 minutes, then the shrimp and mussels and cook 4 minutes more until the shells open and the fish just flakes. Add the most delicate fish last.
Serve the broth and fish in wide bowls with toasted baguette spread thickly with rouille floated on top.

title: Mussels in White Wine
description: Mussels steamed open in wine, garlic and butter in under fifteen minutes.
steps: Scrub the mussels and pull off any beards. Discard any that are cracked, or that stay open when you tap them firmly - those are dead.
Cook the shallots in the butter and oil 4 minutes, then add the garlic and pepper flakes for 1 minute.
Add the wine, bring to a hard boil and let it cook 2 minutes to drive off the raw alcohol.
Tip in the mussels, cover tightly and steam 5-7 minutes, shaking the pot once, until they have opened.
Lift the mussels into bowls and discard any that stayed shut. Stir the cream and salt into the broth and let it bubble 1 minute.
Pour the broth over, add a lot of parsley, and serve with lemon and bread. The broth is the best part, so give everyone a spoon.

title: Mediterranean Orzo Salad
description: Orzo tossed with feta, olives, cucumber and a lemon-oregano dressing.
steps: Cook the orzo in well-salted water until just past al dente, then rinse under cold water and drain thoroughly. Rinsing stops it clumping into a solid block as it cools.
Whisk the oil, lemon juice, vinegar, garlic, oregano, salt and pepper.
Toss the drained orzo with half the dressing while it is still slightly warm so it absorbs rather than just wearing it.
Cool 20 minutes, then fold in the cucumber, tomatoes, olives and red onion.
Add the feta and herbs and the rest of the dressing.
Chill 1 hour. Taste again before serving - cold pasta salad always needs more salt and lemon than you expect.

title: Za'atar Roasted Vegetables
description: A sheet pan of vegetables roasted hard and dusted with za'atar.
ingredients: 1 red bell pepper, cut in strips
steps: Heat the oven to 450F with two sheet pans inside. A preheated pan starts browning the moment the vegetables land.
Toss all the vegetables with the oil, salt and pepper.
Spread them across both hot pans in a single layer with space between - two pans rather than one crowded pan is the whole trick.
Roast 30-35 minutes, turning once, until charred at the edges and tender.
Toss the hot vegetables with the za'atar and lemon juice. Adding za'atar after roasting keeps its sesame and thyme from burning.
Finish with parsley and feta.

title: Fasolakia
description: Green beans braised soft in olive oil and tomato. Not crisp, and that is correct.
steps: Cook the onions in the olive oil over medium heat 10 minutes until soft. Use all the oil - this is a ladera dish, meaning cooked in oil, and the oil becomes the sauce.
Add the garlic for 1 minute, then the beans and potatoes and stir to coat.
Add the tomatoes, water, salt, pepper and sugar and bring to a simmer.
Cover and cook 35-40 minutes until the beans are completely soft and olive-colored. Do not aim for bright green and crisp - braised-soft is the whole character of fasolakia.
Uncover for the last 10 minutes so the sauce reduces and the oil rises to the surface.
Stir in the herbs and serve warm or at room temperature with feta and bread.

title: Gigantes Plaki
description: Giant white beans baked in tomato, dill and olive oil until creamy.
ingredients: 1 lb dried gigantes or lima beans, soaked overnight
steps: Soak the beans overnight, then simmer them in fresh unsalted water 50-60 minutes until just tender but not falling apart. Salting the cooking water now would toughen the skins.
Cook the onions and celery in the oil 10 minutes, then add the garlic and tomato paste for 2 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, water, oregano, pepper flakes, salt and honey and simmer 10 minutes.
Fold in the drained beans and half the dill, then pour everything into a baking dish. The beans should be just submerged.
Bake uncovered at 350F for 75-90 minutes, until the top beans have browned and the sauce is thick and glossy with oil on the surface.
Stir in the rest of the dill and the parsley, top with feta and serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Beet and Walnut Salad
description: Roasted beets with yogurt, toasted walnuts and dill.
steps: Wrap the whole unpeeled beets in foil with a splash of water and roast at 400F for 50-60 minutes, until a knife slides in easily. Roasting them whole and wrapped concentrates their sweetness instead of leaching it into water.
Cool slightly, then rub the skins off with a paper towel - they slip off easily while warm and stain much less.
Cut into wedges and toss with the olive oil, salt and half the lemon juice.
Stir the yogurt with the garlic, the rest of the lemon juice and a pinch of salt and spread it across a platter.
Pile the beets on top, keeping some yogurt visible rather than mixing it all together.
Scatter the walnuts, dill and pomegranate seeds over and drizzle with pomegranate molasses and black pepper.

title: Gemista
description: Tomatoes and peppers stuffed with herbed rice and baked over potatoes.
steps: Slice the tops off the tomatoes and peppers and keep them as lids. Scoop out the tomato flesh, chop it and reserve - it goes into the filling.
Cook the onions in half the oil 10 minutes, add the garlic, then the chopped tomato flesh, tomato paste, sugar and herbs. Simmer 10 minutes.
Stir in the uncooked rice, salt and pepper. The rice swells considerably, so fill the vegetables only two thirds full or they will split.
Stand the stuffed vegetables in a roasting pan, replace the lids and tuck the potato wedges into the gaps.
Pour over the remaining oil and the water, cover with foil and bake at 375F for 50 minutes.
Uncover and bake 25-30 minutes more until the tops are browned and the rice is tender. Rest 15 minutes and serve warm or at room temperature with feta.

title: Farro Salad with Herbs
description: Chewy farro with cucumber, herbs, feta and a lemon dressing.
steps: Simmer the farro in the salted water 25-30 minutes until tender but still chewy, then drain well. Pearled farro cooks fastest; whole farro needs longer and a soak.
Spread it on a sheet pan to cool quickly - left in a pot it keeps steaming and goes soft.
Whisk the oil, lemon juice, garlic, Dijon, salt and pepper.
Toss the warm farro with half the dressing so it absorbs the flavor.
Once cool, fold in the cucumber, tomatoes, onion, herbs and the rest of the dressing.
Add the feta and almonds just before serving so the nuts stay crunchy.

title: Mediterranean Chickpea Salad
description: Two cans of chickpeas, chopped vegetables and lemon. Ten minutes, no cooking.
ingredients: 2 cans (15 oz each) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
steps: Rinse the chickpeas well and pat them dry - canning liquid tastes tinny and makes the salad cloudy.
Whisk the oil, lemon juice, garlic, oregano, salt and pepper.
Combine the chickpeas, cucumber, tomatoes, onion, bell pepper and herbs in a large bowl.
Pour the dressing over and toss well.
Fold in the feta and olives last so the feta stays in pieces.
Best after 30 minutes in the fridge, and it holds for three days - though the cucumber softens, so add it fresh if making ahead.

title: Grilled Halloumi Salad
description: Seared halloumi over greens with watermelon, mint and lemon.
ingredients: 2 tbsp olive oil, for the cheese
steps: Pat the halloumi slices completely dry - any surface moisture steams instead of searing.
Brush with oil and cook in a very hot dry grill pan 2 minutes per side, until dark grill marks form and the cheese softens inside. Halloumi does not melt, which is what makes it grillable.
Whisk the remaining oil, lemon juice, honey, salt and pepper.
Toss the arugula, watermelon, cucumber, onion and mint with most of the dressing.
Lay the hot halloumi over the top and drizzle with the rest.
Scatter the pistachios and serve immediately, while the cheese is still warm and squeaky.

title: Lamb Chops with Rosemary
description: Rib chops seared hard with garlic, rosemary and lemon.
steps: Mix the oil, garlic, rosemary, lemon juice, salt and pepper and rub it over the chops. Leave them at room temperature 30 minutes - cold chops cook unevenly in the short time they need.
Scrape most of the garlic off before cooking; it burns at searing heat and turns acrid.
Get a heavy skillet very hot. Sear the chops 2-3 minutes per side for medium-rare, working in batches so the pan stays hot.
Stand them on their fat edge for 1 minute to render and crisp it.
Add the butter and the scraped-off garlic and rosemary in the last minute and baste the chops with the foaming butter.
Rest 5 minutes and serve with lemon wedges and the pan butter spooned over.

title: Roast Leg of Lamb
description: Garlic and herb studded leg roasted over potatoes for Easter.
ingredients: 4 lb Yukon gold potatoes, cut in wedges
steps: Pat the lamb dry and cut 20 small deep slits all over it. Push a sliver of garlic and a pinch of rosemary into each one - studding it this way seasons the interior, not just the surface.
Rub the outside with half the oil, the lemon juice, oregano, salt and pepper. Rest at room temperature 1 hour.
Toss the potatoes with the remaining oil and salt in a large roasting pan and pour in the broth.
Set the lamb on a rack over the potatoes so the fat drips onto them, and tuck the lemon halves in.
Roast at 450F for 20 minutes, then lower to 350F and roast about 1 3/4 hours, to 135F internal for medium. Use a thermometer in the thickest part away from the bone.
Rest the lamb a full 20 minutes before carving, loosely tented. Serve with the potatoes and pan juices.

title: Spanish Tortilla
description: A thick potato and onion omelette, cooked slowly and flipped once.
ingredients: 2 lb Yukon gold potatoes, sliced thin
steps: Warm the oil in a 10-inch nonstick skillet over medium-low and add the potatoes and onions with 1 tsp of the salt. They should be submerged.
Poach them gently 20-25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until completely tender. They must not brown - this is a confit, not a fry.
Drain them in a sieve, saving the oil for next time.
Beat the eggs with the rest of the salt and the pepper, then fold in the warm potatoes and let the mixture sit 10 minutes so the potatoes absorb some egg.
Heat 2 tbsp of the saved oil in the pan, pour the mixture in and cook over medium-low 8-10 minutes, shaking occasionally, until the edges set and the center is still loose.

Slide it onto a plate, invert the pan over it and flip the whole thing back in. Cook 4-5 minutes more. The center should stay slightly soft - a dry tortilla is an overcooked one. Serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Ratatouille
description: Provencal summer vegetables cooked separately, then simmered together.
steps: Cook each vegetable separately in batches in the olive oil over medium-high heat: the eggplant 8 minutes, the zucchini 5, the peppers 6. Set each aside as it finishes. Cooking them together makes a uniform mush; separately, each keeps its own character.
Cook the onion in the same pan 8 minutes, then the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, tomato paste, herbes de Provence, bay leaves, salt and pepper and simmer 15 minutes.
Return all the vegetables and simmer gently 15-20 minutes, stirring as little as possible.
Fish out the bay leaves and stir in the vinegar - it lifts the whole dish out of sweetness.
Fold in the basil off the heat. Serve warm or at room temperature; it is better the next day.

title: Pan con Tomate
description: Grilled bread rubbed with garlic and raw grated tomato. Four ingredients.
steps: Grate the tomatoes on the large holes of a box grater, holding the cut side against the blade, until only the skin is left in your hand. Grating rather than chopping gives you pulp that soaks in.
Drain the pulp briefly in a sieve so the bread does not go soggy.
Grill or broil the bread until well charred at the edges but still chewy inside.
Rub a cut garlic clove firmly over each hot slice. The rough toast works like a grater, and the heat takes the raw edge off.
Spoon the tomato pulp over, pour olive oil on generously and finish with flaky salt.
Eat within minutes. This dish lives or dies on ripe tomatoes and good oil, so use the best of both you have.

title: Gazpacho
description: Chilled raw tomato soup emulsified with olive oil and bread.
ingredients: 2 slices stale white bread, crusts removed
steps: Soak the bread in a little water for 5 minutes, then squeeze it out. The bread is what gives gazpacho its body and keeps the oil emulsified rather than floating on top.
Blend the tomatoes, cucumber, pepper, onion, garlic and soaked bread until completely smooth, working in batches if needed.
With the blender running, pour in the olive oil in a thin stream. The soup should turn opaque and pale orange - that color change means the emulsion took.
Add the vinegar, salt and pepper and blend once more.
For the classic silky texture, pass it through a fine sieve, pressing with a ladle.
Chill at least 3 hours. Taste again cold - it will need more salt and vinegar than it did warm. Serve with diced cucumber, chives and a last drizzle of oil.

title: Patatas Bravas
description: Crisp fried potato cubes under smoky brava sauce and aioli.
ingredients: 3 lb russet potatoes, cut in 1-inch cubes
3 tbsp olive oil, for the sauce
2 cloves garlic, minced, for the aioli
steps: Make the brava sauce: cook the onion in 3 tbsp oil 8 minutes, add the garlic, smoked paprika, cayenne and tomato paste for 2 minutes, then the tomatoes and vinegar. Simmer 20 minutes and blend smooth.
Stir the mayonnaise with the extra garlic and lemon juice for the aioli.
Fry the potato cubes in 275F oil for 12 minutes until tender but pale, then lift them out and let them cool 10 minutes. This double-fry is what gives a crisp shell and a fluffy interior.
Raise the oil to 375F and fry them again, 4-5 minutes, until deep golden and crunchy.
Drain on a rack and salt immediately.
Pile the potatoes on a platter, spoon the warm brava sauce over and zigzag the aioli on top. Finish with parsley and serve at once.

title: Mediterranean Chicken Bake
description: Chicken thighs roasted on one pan with tomatoes, olives, feta and lemon.
steps: Heat the oven to 425F. Whisk the oil, lemon juice, garlic, oregano, pepper flakes, salt and pepper.
Toss the tomatoes, onion and olives with half the mixture in a large roasting pan.
Pat the chicken dry, rub it with the rest, and set it skin-side up on top of the vegetables so the skin stays clear of the juices and crisps.
Tuck the lemon slices around and roast 30 minutes.
Scatter the feta cubes among the vegetables and roast 12-15 minutes more, until the thighs read 175F and the tomatoes have burst.
Rest 5 minutes, finish with parsley, and spoon the pan juices over everything.

title: Braised Lamb Shanks with Chickpeas
description: Shanks braised three hours with cinnamon, tomato and chickpeas.
steps: Season the shanks and brown them hard in the oil on all sides, 10 minutes total, working in batches. This crust is the base of the whole braise.
Cook the onions and carrots 10 minutes, then add the garlic, tomato paste and all the spices for 2 minutes.
Add the wine and reduce by half, scraping the pot clean.
Return the shanks with the tomatoes and broth - the liquid should come about two thirds up the meat, not cover it.
Cover and braise at 325F for 2 1/2 hours, then add the chickpeas and cook 30 minutes more, until the meat pulls away from the bone with no resistance.
Skim the fat from the surface, then finish with cilantro and lemon zest stirred in at the table. That raw brightness cuts three hours of richness.

title: Vegetable Moussaka
description: Meatless moussaka with lentils and mushrooms under bechamel.
steps: Salt the eggplant slices, drain 45 minutes, pat dry, brush with oil and roast at 425F for 25 minutes until golden.
Cook the onions and mushrooms in oil over high heat 12 minutes until browned and dry - the mushrooms must lose their water or the filling will be loose.
Add the garlic, lentils, tomato paste, tomatoes, broth and spices and simmer 35-40 minutes until the lentils are tender and the mixture is thick enough to mound on a spoon.
Make a thick bechamel with the butter, flour and warm milk, season with nutmeg, then cool 5 minutes and whisk in the egg yolks and half the Parmesan.
Layer in a deep dish: eggplant, lentil filling, eggplant, then all the bechamel. Top with the rest of the Parmesan.
Bake at 350F for 50-60 minutes until deep golden and set. Rest 45 minutes before cutting.

title: Briam
description: Greek roasted vegetables in olive oil - slow, soft and deeply caramelized.
steps: Heat the oven to 400F. Whisk the tomato paste with the water, olive oil, oregano, salt and pepper.
Arrange all the sliced vegetables in a large roasting pan, overlapping them in rows or just tossed together, with the garlic tucked throughout.
Pour the oil mixture over and toss with your hands so everything is coated. Use all the oil - briam is cooked in oil, and skimping gives you dry vegetables.
Roast 50 minutes, then stir gently and press the vegetables back into an even layer.
Roast 35-40 minutes more until the edges are browned and the vegetables are completely soft. They should look collapsed, not crisp.
Rest 15 minutes, then finish with parsley and feta. Serve warm or at room temperature with bread.

title: Bulgur Pilaf
description: Coarse bulgur cooked with tomato and pepper. Faster than rice.
steps: Cook the onion and bell pepper in the butter and oil 8 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic, tomato paste, Aleppo pepper and cumin and cook 2 minutes until the paste darkens.
Add the bulgur and stir 2 minutes to coat every grain in fat - this keeps the pilaf fluffy rather than porridgy.
Pour in the broth, add the salt and bring to a boil.
Cover, lower the heat to the minimum and cook 15 minutes, then take it off the heat and rest, still covered, 10 minutes.
Fluff with a fork and fold in the parsley and scallions.

title: Warm Marinated Olives
description: Mixed olives warmed in citrus oil with garlic, rosemary and chile.
steps: Rinse and thoroughly drain the olives so they are not overly briny.
Warm the oil with the garlic, rosemary, both zests, fennel seeds, pepper flakes and bay leaves over low heat for 8 minutes. Keep the heat low - you are infusing the oil, not frying the aromatics.
Add the olives and warm them through 5 minutes, stirring. They should be hot but not sizzling.
Take off the heat and stir in the vinegar.
Serve warm, or let them cool and refrigerate up to two weeks - they get better with time.
Bring them back to room temperature before serving, since cold oil congeals and dulls the flavor.

title: Mediterranean Grain Bowl
description: Quinoa or farro with hummus, roasted vegetables, feta and tahini.
steps: Rinse the quinoa well - the coating is bitter if you skip this - then cook it in the salted water, covered, 15 minutes. Rest 5 minutes off the heat and fluff.
Toss the chickpeas, zucchini, onion and tomatoes with the oil, cumin and a pinch of salt.
Roast at 425F for 30-35 minutes until browned at the edges and the chickpeas have crisped.
Build each bowl in sections rather than mixing: a bed of quinoa, a swoosh of hummus up one side, then the roasted vegetables.
Add the cucumber, olives, feta and parsley in their own areas so each bite can be different.
Drizzle with tahini sauce, dust with za'atar and serve with lemon wedges. Keep components separate in the fridge for meal prep.

title: Fried Eggplant with Yogurt
description: Golden fried eggplant slices under garlic yogurt and mint.
steps: Salt the eggplant slices and leave them in a colander 30 minutes, then press them dry between paper towels. This both removes bitterness and keeps them from drinking the whole pan of oil.
Stir the yogurt with the garlic, lemon juice and salt and let it sit at room temperature.
Fry the slices in batches in the hot oil, 3-4 minutes per side, until deep golden and completely soft.
Drain on a rack, not paper towels, so they do not steam and go limp.
Spread the garlic yogurt across a platter and overlap the warm eggplant on top.
Scatter the mint, pine nuts, sumac and Aleppo pepper over and finish with a drizzle of olive oil.

title: Baklava
description: Phyllo layered with nuts and soaked in syrup. Hot pastry, cool syrup.
steps: Make the syrup first so it has time to cool: simmer the 2 cups sugar, water, honey, lemon zest and cinnamon stick for 12 minutes, then add the lemon juice and orange blossom water and cool completely. The temperature difference between hot pastry and cool syrup is what makes baklava crisp rather than soggy.
Pulse the nuts with the 1/2 cup sugar, cinnamon and cloves into a coarse crumble - not a powder.
Butter a 9x13 pan and layer 10 sheets of phyllo, brushing each with butter. Keep the rest under a damp towel.
Add a third of the nuts, then 5 buttered sheets, then another third, 5 more sheets, the last of the nuts, and finally 10 buttered sheets on top.
Cut all the way through into diamonds before baking. You cannot cut it cleanly afterwards.
Bake at 325F for 1 hour 15 minutes until deep golden throughout. Pour the cool syrup over the hot baklava immediately - it will hiss. Rest at least 4 hours, uncovered, before serving.

title: Galaktoboureko
description: Semolina custard baked in phyllo and drenched in lemon syrup.
steps: Make the syrup and cool it completely: simmer the 2 cups sugar, water, lemon zest strips and cinnamon stick 12 minutes, add the lemon juice and chill.
Heat the milk, then rain in the semolina while whisking constantly and cook 8-10 minutes until very thick. Adding semolina slowly while whisking is the only way to avoid lumps.
Off the heat, beat in the sugar, butter, vanilla, lemon zest and salt, then the eggs one at a time, whisking hard so they do not scramble. Cool 15 minutes.
Butter a 9x13 pan and layer 8 buttered phyllo sheets with overhang, pour in the custard, fold the overhang over and top with 8 more buttered sheets.
Score the top layers into squares and bake at 350F for 55-65 minutes until deep golden and set.
Pour the cold syrup over the hot pastry immediately, all of it. Rest at least 4 hours before cutting; it needs that time to absorb and set.

title: Greek Yogurt with Honey and Walnuts
description: Three ingredients, five minutes, and better than most desserts.
steps: Toast the walnuts in a dry pan over medium heat 4 minutes, shaking often, until they smell nutty. Cool them so they stay crunchy.
Use full-fat strained yogurt, not low-fat. The whole appeal here is the contrast between thick, tart yogurt and sweet honey.
Spoon the yogurt into bowls and smooth the surface.
Chop the cooled walnuts roughly and scatter them over.
Pour the honey on generously and finish with cinnamon and lemon zest.

title: Basbousa
description: Semolina cake soaked in syrup, topped with almonds and coconut.
steps: Make the syrup first: simmer the 1 1/2 cups sugar with the water for 10 minutes, then add the lemon juice and rose water and leave it to cool.
Mix the semolina, coconut, sugar, baking powder and salt, then stir in the yogurt, melted butter and vanilla into a thick batter.
Let the batter rest 15 minutes so the semolina hydrates. This is what stops the finished cake being gritty.
Spread it in a buttered 9x13 pan and smooth the top. Score it into diamonds and press an almond into the center of each.
Bake at 350F for 35-40 minutes until golden brown at the edges and firm in the center.
Pour the cooled syrup over the hot cake, all of it. It will look like far too much; it absorbs within an hour. Rest 2 hours before cutting along the scored lines.

title: Loukoumades
description: Greek doughnut holes fried crisp and drowned in honey syrup.
steps: Whisk the flour, warm water, yeast, sugar, salt and olive oil into a very loose, sticky batter - closer to a thick pancake batter than a dough. Do not add more flour.
Cover and let it rise 1 1/2 hours until bubbly and doubled.
Warm the honey with the 1/2 cup water, cinnamon stick and lemon juice for 5 minutes, then keep it warm.
Heat 3 inches of oil to 350F. Scoop the batter with a wet spoon or squeeze it between your thumb and forefinger into rough balls, dropping them straight into the oil.
Fry 3-4 minutes, turning, until deep golden and hollow-sounding. They puff and turn themselves.
Drain briefly, then drop the hot loukoumades straight into the warm syrup and turn to coat. Pile them up and finish with walnuts and cinnamon. Eat immediately.

title: Knafeh
description: Shredded phyllo over melting cheese, soaked in syrup and inverted.
ingredients: 1 lb akkawi or low-moisture mozzarella, shredded and soaked
steps: If using akkawi, soak the shredded cheese in cold water for 2 hours, changing the water three times, to draw out the salt. Taste it - it should be mild, or the dessert will be savory.
Make the syrup: simmer the sugar and water 12 minutes, add the lemon juice and orange blossom water and cool.
Pull the kataifi apart with your fingers into loose strands and toss it thoroughly with the melted butter, rubbing it in so every strand is coated.
Press half the buttered kataifi firmly into a buttered round pan. Mix the cheeses with the semolina and spread it over, then top with the remaining kataifi, pressing down hard.
Bake at 400F for 45-50 minutes until the top is deep golden and the edges pull away from the pan.
Pour the cool syrup over the hot knafeh, wait 2 minutes, then invert onto a platter in one confident motion. Scatter the pistachios over the top and serve warm, while the cheese still pulls.

title: Tahini Halva
description: Sesame paste set with sugar syrup into a dense, flaky sweet.
steps: Stir the tahini thoroughly to recombine the oil, then warm it gently in a bowl to about body temperature. Cold tahini will seize when the hot syrup hits it.
Boil the sugar and water to 250F on a candy thermometer, about 8 minutes. This temperature is not negotiable: too low and the halva never sets, too high and it turns hard and grainy.
Pour the hot syrup into the warm tahini and stir with a spatula.

Stir in the vanilla and salt, then keep folding for 2-3 minutes. The mixture will thicken and start to pull away from the bowl - stop as soon as it looks like it is about to separate, because over-stirring makes it oily.
Fold in half the pistachios, scrape into a parchment-lined loaf pan and press flat.
Drizzle with the melted chocolate and scatter the rest of the pistachios. Refrigerate 2 hours, then slice thin. It keeps a month.

title: Orange Blossom Fruit Salad
description: Citrus and melon with orange blossom water, mint and pistachios.
steps: Segment the oranges over a bowl so you catch the juice, cutting away all the white pith - it is bitter and spoils the clean flavor.
Whisk the collected juice with the honey, orange blossom water and lemon juice. Go easy on the orange blossom water; it is powerful, and too much tastes like perfume.
Combine all the fruit in a wide bowl and pour the dressing over.
Chill 30 minutes so the flavors mingle, no longer or the strawberries go soft.
Fold in most of the mint just before serving.
Top with pistachios, pomegranate seeds and the rest of the mint.

title: Turkish Coffee
description: Ultra-fine coffee simmered in a cezve and poured grounds and all.
steps: Use coffee ground to a powder as fine as flour. Regular espresso grind will not work - it sinks and tastes thin.
Put the cold water, coffee, sugar and cardamom in a cezve or small pot and stir once to combine, then do not stir again.
Heat over low heat. Patience is everything here: it should take 4-5 minutes to come up, and rushing it kills the foam.
Watch for a dark foam rising up the sides. Just before it boils over, lift the pot off the heat.
Spoon a little of that foam into each cup, then return the pot to the heat for 20 seconds and pour the rest in slowly.
Let it stand 1 minute so the grounds settle to the bottom, and drink without stirring. Never drink the last sip.

title: Greek Frappe
description: Instant coffee shaken into a thick foam and poured over ice.
steps: Put the instant coffee, sugar and the 1/4 cup cold water in a cocktail shaker or tall jar with a lid.
Shake hard for 30-45 seconds until it builds a thick, pale, mousse-like foam. Instant coffee is required - ground coffee will not foam, and this is the one drink where instant is the correct choice.
Fill two tall glasses with ice.
Pour the foam over the ice, dividing it between the glasses.
Top slowly with cold water and the milk, pouring down the side so the foam stays on top.
Serve with a straw and do not stir - you drink it through the foam.
